+Also: `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass` implement `Hash`, `ErrorCode` implements `Display` (its label), and `DomainError` implements `PartialEq`.

+michi-pipeline: `StepId` and `RunId` implement `FromStr` and `Borrow<str>`, so `"fetch".parse::<StepId>()` works and a map keyed by id can be looked up with a `&str`. `AttemptRecord` implements `Eq`. `RunRecord::to_pipeline()` no longer carries the run id (read it with `run_id()`). An ambiguous timeout's `DomainError` now carries one verify-first hint, not none: the conversion used to write `retryable = false` past the builder and so dropped core's hint.

+michi-node: Breaking: `renderPartialSuccess` takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]` in place of `OpRef[]`. +michi-core: every outcome composes into one `AgentResponse`. `error(DomainError)` adds the error block, which renders first, and `partial_success(name, ps)`, `status(s)`, `pipeline(name, p)` and `already_done(operation, summary)` add sections. Their hints and recovery hints join the response's one `help` and `recovery` block. A batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is now one valid TOON document, one JSON object and one MCP result. NAPI: `AgentResponse` gains `error`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `alreadyDone`, so `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` now cover errors too.

content.text:
**Rust and crates:** Rust is current. michi tracks `stable`, so CI already builds with 1.100.0, the latest. This machine is on 1.99.1 (`rustup update` fixes that), and the MSRV stays at 1.93. No direct dependency has a newer major version, but the lockfiles were behind: 24 crates in the main lockfile and 5 in the fuzz one, including `napi` 3.15→3.16.2 and `napi-derive` 3.6→3.7.1. I updated both in PR #139 (https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/pull/139). The 1.93 MSRV build, `just check` and `just test` all pass (1,224 Rust and 186 Node tests).

**Callisto 0.22:** the research is back, and the config part is easy but the workflow part isn't.

- **Config:** `callisto.toml` drops from 38 lines to about 10. `[changesets]`, `[cascade]` and `release-trigger` are all defaults now. The new `[release] targets` block is for Rust binaries, so michi doesn't need it; napi platforms still come from `package.json`.
- **Workflow:** 0.22 tells you to regenerate it with `callisto init --workflow`. Doing that as-is would publish a broken npm package: the generated build skips `index.js`/`index.d.ts`, so the tarball ships without its loader. It would also drop four things:
  - the attestation verification
  - the check that only a merged version PR can release
  - manual recovery of a stuck release
  - the post-publish smoke test

  The safe route is to edit our existing workflow to 0.22's new rules: build and pack without credentials, publish only sealed artifacts, and run `npm publish --ignore-scripts`. That means adding new packing and attestation jobs.
- **Other 0.21–0.22 breaking changes:** none affect michi.
- **Timing:** if the upgrade merges before #131, Callisto rebuilds the release PR, and 0.11.0 becomes the very first run of a rewritten workflow whose publishes can't be undone. The research agent recommends releasing 0.11.0 on 0.20 first.

A `RetryConfig` can no longer get a zero `max_delay` after `try_new`, which turned a server's `Retry-After: 60` into an immediate retry. A `DomainError` can no longer have its code or retry flag changed behind the builder, which left a retryable timeout without its "verify first" hint. A `PartialSuccess` can no longer list one operation as both completed and failed. `CallToolResult.structured_content` is now an `Option<JsonObject>`, checked when it is built in every build, so every result serializes. The wire output is unchanged.

-Breaking: `DomainError`'s fields are private. Read them with `code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()` and `is_retryable()`, and use `class()` to classify. `render()` and `render_json()` are now `render(OutputFormat::Text)` and `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. `retry_after` takes `impl Into<Option<Duration>>`, and the new `context(prefix)` replaces writing to `message`. `michi_core::Error` and `michi_core::Result` are removed; nothing in michi produced them. `RetryConfig`'s fields are private; read them with `max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()` and `jitter_factor()`, and build one with `new`, `try_new` or `default`. `PartialSuccess::new` is now `PartialSuccess::try_new`, which returns `DuplicateOpIndex` when an index repeats. Its fields are read with `completed()`, `failed()` and `skipped()`. `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason) and `SkippedOp`. `Pipeline` has no `id`, so `Pipeline::new(steps)` takes only the steps. `CallToolResult::new` takes `Option<JsonObject>`; `CallToolResult::try_new` is removed (use `JsonObject::try_new`). `StatusResponse::with_hints` is renamed `hints`, and `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]`.
-Also: `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass` implement `Hash`, `ErrorCode` implements `Display` (its label), and `DomainError` implements `PartialEq`.

An ambiguous timeout's `DomainError` now carries one verify-first hint, not none: the conversion used to write `retryable = false` past the builder and so dropped core's hint.

-michi-node: Breaking: `renderPartialSuccess` takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]` in place of `OpRef[]`. It throws when an `index` appears twice across the three lists, and when a completed operation has a `reason`. Before, a duplicate rendered as two outcomes and the reason was dropped without a word.

Replace `e.render()` with `e.render(OutputFormat::Text)`, and replace `cfg.max_delay` and the other config fields with `cfg.max_delay()`. Their hints and recovery hints join the response's one `help` and `recovery` block. A batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is now one valid TOON document, one JSON object and one MCP result. _2026-11-21 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/compare/michi-node@0.10.0...michi-node@0.11.0)_

### Minor Changes

- `AgentResponse` can now hold every kind of outcome, so a batch with results, per-operation outcomes and an error is one valid TOON document, one JSON object and one MCP result.

  - New methods: `error`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `alreadyDone`. `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` now cover errors too.
  - Their hints and recovery hints join the response's single `help` and `recovery` block.
  - A response with an error and an invalid section reports both on every output: your error leads and stays the JSON `error`, and each validation failure follows its causes as `toon_validation_failed: <message>` (or `kv_validation_failed`). `isError` stays true.
- **Breaking:** the input limit per call, and per `AgentResponse`, is now 16 MiB, down from 64 MiB.

  - Over the limit, a call throws `input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` or `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216`, and the builder is unchanged. Split larger content across calls or trim it.
  - Why: output can be many times larger than input (escaping, repeated names), and at 64 MiB a response could take gigabytes to render or fail only after rendering. Now an oversized response is rejected up front.
  - Long cells and repeated names count toward the limit wherever the output repeats them. Typical responses (short names, cells under 200 chars) are charged about the same as before.
- **Breaking:** the JSON from `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult().structuredContent` changes in two places.

  - A validation failure is now an `error` object, `{"code": "toon_validation_failed", "message": …, "causes": [], "retryable": false}` (or `kv_validation_failed`). Before it was `isError: true` with no `error` object. The text is unchanged.
  - A section's `totalCount` appears when the total is larger than the rows returned, is `0` for an empty list, and is left out otherwise (before, it was whatever total you passed).
- **Breaking:** `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint now belong to `AgentResponse`, which places each once for the whole response. The older standalone parameters and functions are removed.

  - `renderToon` no longer takes `totalCount`, `hints` or `truncationHint`, and `renderKv(items)` no longer takes `totalCount` or `hints`. `AgentResponse.items`, `kvItems` and `truncationHint` keep them: use those to attach them.
  - `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed. Use `new AgentResponse(name)` (plus `.hint(..)`).
  - An empty list now renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0` (it rendered `name: []` alone), also from `renderPipeline` (`step: []`) and `renderStatus` (`items: []`).
- **Breaking:** `renderPartialSuccess` renders one table and checks its input harder.

  - Before: a quoted summary line, then separate `completed`, `failed` and `skipped` tables. Now: `partial_success[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, one row per operation sorted by index. An empty report renders `partial_success: []` and `totalCount: 0`. Anything that parses the old text must read the new table.
  - It takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]` in place of `OpRef[]`.
  - It throws when an `index` appears twice across the three lists, and when a completed operation has a `reason`. Before, a duplicate rendered as two outcomes and the reason was dropped without a word.
- **Breaking:** `renderToon`, `renderKv` and `kvItems` now reject more names, so caller data cannot pose as michi's own keys.

  - `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code` join `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery` and `truncated` as reserved, as a list type name or a key-value key. The error message lists the reserved keys.
  - Rename any key or list type that matches one, for example a `message` field becomes `commit_message`.

## 0.11.0

_2026-11-21 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/compare/michi-pipeline@0.10.0...michi-pipeline@0.11.0)_

### Minor Changes

- **Breaking:** `DurableObserver::record_start` for parallel steps now runs concurrently, so their saves overlap instead of queuing.

  - Before: start markers were saved one after another in the scheduler loop. Now each step saves its own, so `record_start` must be safe to call concurrently and in any order across steps. Make your implementation thread-safe.
  - A step still runs only after its own `record_start` returns `Ok`. A cancel or fail-fast stop during the save ends the step `Skipped(Cancelled)`.
  - A deadline group's window now opens before the first step's save, so the save counts against it. A step whose window ends during its save ends `Failed` with `DeadlinePassed` (the same message as a window that ends before dispatch) without being invoked.
  - A step that ends during its save was never invoked, so its record has no `started_at` or `elapsed`.
- **Breaking:** converting an `ExecutionError` to a `DomainError` no longer puts step text in the trusted `message`.

  - Before: `message` carried what the step or server said. Now: `message` is fixed text (`http 502`, `the step reported an error`, `step panicked`, `deadline passed`) after the step context `step <id> (<name>) failed: `.
  - What the step or server said (an HTTP body, a `failed()` message, a panic payload) is one entry in `causes`, redacted and cut to 512 bytes including the `…` marker. Read it from `causes`, not `message`.
  - An ambiguous timeout's `DomainError` now carries its "verify first" hint (it carried none before).
- **Breaking:** `RunRecord::to_pipeline()` no longer carries the run id (read it with `run_id()`), and `RunRecord::render` of a run with no steps now renders `step: []` and `totalCount: 0`.

  Also new: `StepId` and `RunId` implement `FromStr` and `Borrow<str>`, so `"fetch".parse::<StepId>()` works and a map keyed by id can be looked up with a `&str`. `AttemptRecord` implements `Eq`.

### Patch Changes

- A step that never ran no longer reports a run time: a step refused by an open breaker, or cancelled before it started, now has no `started_at` or `elapsed` in its record. Before, both showed how long the step waited.

lines: +**Breaking:** types that have a rule across their fields now keep those fields private, so the rule holds for the value's whole life.
+- A `RetryConfig` can no longer get a zero `max_delay` after `try_new` (that turned a server's `Retry-After: 60` into an immediate retry).
+- A `DomainError` can no longer have its code or retry flag changed behind the builder (that left a retryable timeout without its "verify first" hint).
+- `CallToolResult.structured_content` is an `Option<JsonObject>`, checked when it is built in every build, so every result serializes.
+- `TruncationOutcome`'s total can never fall below the items kept.

+- `DomainError`: read fields with `code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()` and `is_retryable()`; classify with `class()`. `render()` and `render_json()` become `render(OutputFormat::Text)` and `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. `retry_after` takes `impl Into<Option<Duration>>`. Use the new `context(prefix)` instead of writing to `message`.
+- `michi_core::Error` and `michi_core::Result` are removed; nothing in michi produced them. Replace `michi_core::Error::Domain(e)` with `e`.
+- `RetryConfig`: read with `max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()` and `jitter_factor()`; build with `new`, `try_new` or `default`.

+- `TruncationOutcome`: `outcome.kept` becomes `outcome.kept()` (or `into_kept()` to take the items), `outcome.total_before` becomes `total_before()`. Build one with `new`, `truncate_by_count` or `truncate_by_size` as before.
+- `CallToolResult::new` takes `Option<JsonObject>`: wrap structured content as `Some(JsonObject::try_new(text)?)`. `CallToolResult::try_new` is removed.
+- The `telemetry` module and its `NoopProvider` are removed (nothing used them).

+Also new: `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass` implement `Hash`; `ErrorCode` implements `Display` (its label) and `FromStr` (error type `UnknownErrorCode`) and has `ALL`; `StepStatus` has `ALL` and `from_labels` (error type `StepLabelError`); `DomainError` implements `PartialEq`; `JsonObject` has `as_str()` and `into_string()`. `AgentResponse::new`, `StatusResponse::new`, `Hint::new` and `IdempotencyKey::new` are `#[must_use]`.
+One `AgentResponse` can now hold every kind of outcome, so a batch with results, per-operation outcomes and an error is one valid TOON document, one JSON object and one MCP result.
+- `error(DomainError)` adds the error block, which renders first.
+- `partial_success(name, ps)`, `status(s)`, `pipeline(name, p)` and `already_done(operation, summary)` add sections.
+- Their hints and recovery hints join the response's single `help` and `recovery` block.

+- If the response has an error and an invalid section, or two blocks that write the same root key, it reports both on every output (text, JSON, `render_for`, `to_call_tool_result`): your error leads and stays the JSON `error`, and each validation failure follows its causes as `toon_validation_failed: <message>` (or `kv_validation_failed`). `isError` stays true. With several failures and no caller error, the first failure is the `error` and the rest are its causes.

+**Breaking:** `AgentResponse::hints(vec)` now replaces only the hints you added with `hint()` and `hints()`. A `truncated_section()`'s `showing N of M` line is kept (before, `hints()` dropped it), and so are the hints of `status()`, `partial_success()` and `error()` blocks. If you called `hints()` to clear everything, that line and those hints now stay.
+**Breaking:** the JSON your tools return changes in three places.

+- Error JSON: `DomainError::render(OutputFormat::Json)`, its serde form and its `schemars` schema are now the response envelope `{"body", "error": {"code", "message", "causes", "retryable"}, "hints", "recovery", "isError"}`. Before it was `{isError, error, message, causes, retryable, hints, recovery}`, where `error` was the code and `recovery` an object or `null`. Read `error.code` where you read `error`, and `recovery[0]` where you read `recovery` (`recovery` is always an array). The text render is unchanged.

+- Validation failures: a section or key-value failure is now an `error` object, `{"code": "toon_validation_failed", "message": …, "causes": [], "retryable": false}` (or `kv_validation_failed`). Before it was `isError: true` with no `error` object. The text is unchanged.

+- `totalCount` in a section's JSON follows the text's rule: it appears when the total is larger than the rows returned, is `0` for an empty list, and is left out otherwise (before, it was the declared value whenever one was set). The budget roll-up's `total` column follows the same rule. `Section::total()` still returns the value as given.
+**Breaking:** list rendering is now `AgentResponse`'s job, and the older standalone paths are removed so `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint appear once for the whole response.

+- `ToonOptions` describes the list alone: `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` (and their builders) are removed. `render_toon` writes the list and the `truncated` block. `render_kv(items)` loses its `total_count` and `hints` parameters.

+- `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints` and the `empty` module are removed. Use `AgentResponse::new(name)` (plus `.hint(..)`) where you called `empty_state`.

+- One empty list everywhere: an empty `Toon` section (so an untouched `AgentResponse`), an empty `Pipeline` and a `StatusResponse` with no items now render `name: []` and `totalCount: 0` (`step: []` and `items: []` for the last two). Before, an empty `Toon` section rendered `name: []` alone. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing.
+- For hints on a standalone list, use `append_hints(&mut out, &hints)`.

I previewed the whole 0.11.0 release locally with Callisto 0.20.0, the version the release workflow uses, and it's ready once #137 and #138 merge.

- **Versions:** all four packages go from 0.10.0 to 0.11.0.
- **Changelogs:** I ran the real `callisto version` on a throwaway branch (since deleted) and read the output.
  - The npm package's changelog has only the 6 JS entries.

  - michi-core has 8 entries, 6 of them marked breaking.
  - michi-graph gets "released together".
  - No Rust detail leaks into the JS changelog.
- **CI:** #137, #138 and #139 are all green.
- **API cleanup:** removing the duplicate JS renderers (`renderPartialSuccess`, `renderPipeline`, `renderStatus`, `renderAlreadyDone`) doesn't need to block 0.11. Only monokl depends on michi, and it's a Rust crate, so nothing uses those JS functions, and breaking changes are fine before 1.0. I suggest doing it in 0.12.

Yes, I'd release 0.11.0 once #137 and #138 are merged.

**Why now:**
- **It's checked:** the code passed a correctness review, the release notes were checked against the code, and the leftover API was cleaned up. Nothing found blocks the release, and the fixes are in #137 and #138. `just check` and `just test` pass, and CI is green.

- **What's left can wait:** the duplicate JS renderers have no users, so removing them in 0.12 costs nothing.

**Downsides:**
- **Breaking changes:** 0.11 breaks a lot. The only consumer is monokl, which will need the migration either way.
- **GitHub release page:** it will show only michi-core's notes, as 0.10.0 did. The full notes are in each package's CHANGELOG and on crates.io and npm. I can edit the GitHub release page by hand after publishing, or leave it for the Callisto 0.22 fix.

**Steps:**
1. Merge #137, then #138.
2. Wait for Callisto to refresh #131. I'll check its final diff.
3. Merge #131, which publishes to crates.io and npm. I'll then check the smoke test and the published packages.

Commit (conventional, `refactor(core)!: ...`; no session links or Claude-Session trailers) and push the branch (normal push, never force, never main). Do NOT open a PR.

Policy context: pre-1.0, breaking changes are fine and we remove legacy surface instead of shimming. The only consumer of michi is monokl (Rust); it uses none of the items below. Nothing uses the npm package's standalone renderers.

## Remove (NAPI / `@orin-dx/michi`, in crates/michi-core/src/napi/)
- `renderPartialSuccess`, `renderPipeline` (napi/outcome.rs), `renderStatus` (napi/toon.rs), `renderAlreadyDone` and `alreadyDone` (+ the `AlreadyDone` JS object type if it then has no use), and `renderDomainError`. Each duplicates `AgentResponse.partialSuccess/pipeline/status/alreadyDone/error` + `renderText()`.

Validate `code` the same way renderDomainError did; same input limits/budget style as sibling exports.

- `resilience::render_already_done` (~resilience.rs:465) — use `AgentResponse::already_done(operation, summary)` + `.hint`.
- `resilience::already_done(Option<String>) -> AlreadyDone` and the `AlreadyDone` enum (~:439-455), unless something else in the workspace still needs them (check michi-pipeline too); remove their root re-exports in lib.rs.

- Tests: Rust tests, snapshot tests (`cargo insta` — review, don't blindly accept), ui-fail tests, fuzz targets (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/*`), Node tests in packages/michi-node/__test__/ (rewrite coverage of behaviour that still exists through `AgentResponse` methods, e.g. duplicate-index throw via `AgentResponse.partialSuccess`; delete tests only for behaviour that is truly gone), scripts/smoke/*, examples, benches.

- Changesets: follow the project's changeset standard strictly (user-first, per audience). Write TWO new files: `.changeset/js-one-render-path.md` with front matter `michi-node: minor` (JS terms only) and `.changeset/core-one-render-path.md` with `michi-core: minor` (Rust terms only). Each: lead line starting `**Breaking:**` saying what changed for the reader, then short bullets: what was removed → what to use instead (one line each, with a before → after example where useful), and the new `renderGithubAnnotation` in the JS one. execute:
    name: Execute the planned release
    needs: [release-candidate, plan, build, attest, package-cargo, pack-npm]
    # !cancelled() rather than always(): cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job. A skipped job blocks
    # only when it had something to do.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'false')) &&
      (needs.attest.result == 'success' || (needs.attest.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'false')) &&
      (needs.package-cargo.result == 'success' ||
        (needs.package-cargo.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_cargo != 'true')) &&
      (needs.pack-npm.result == 'success' || (needs.pack-npm.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_npm != 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: callisto-release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    outputs:
      smoke_version: ${{ steps.published.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Callisto pushes the release tags from this checkout.
          persist-credentials: true # zizmor: ignore[artipacked]

      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@9234c02c00f65c7b742da4f4dd8b9fdbfbb0215a # callisto@0.22.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.22.0
          verification: require

      # Node and npm from .prototools for `npm publish` and its provenance, rather than the runner image's npm. Nothing
      # is installed or built here: the tarballs were packed without credentials.
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_npm == 'true'
        with:
          cache: 'false'

      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_npm == 'true'
        with:
          name: npm-dist
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets

      - name: Verify the handoff
        run: (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)

      # Records the sha256 of every packed tarball; `release execute` re-checks each one just before it publishes it,
      # and refuses an npm publish the manifest does not seal (E306).
      - name: Write the artifact manifest
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_npm == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" \
            --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" --seal-npm

      # CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN are long-lived secrets because Callisto has no OIDC trusted publishing yet,
      # so they cannot be dropped here. Revisit when it does (the job already holds id-token: write).
      - name: Execute the release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          # Every npm package, @orin-dx/michi included, is now an `npm publish <tarball>`, which honours this.
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Callisto hands this config only to its npm publishers; the token
          # stays an ${NPM_TOKEN} reference, never written to disk.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016
          printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}\n' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/callisto-npmrc"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/callisto-npmrc"
          export CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG="$RUNNER_TEMP/callisto-npmrc"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt"
          args=(--intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
            --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

      # Callisto writes the receipt only after every selected operation succeeded. A registry publish that landed in
      # this run (`published`) or that a re-run adopted from a failed earlier attempt (`alreadySatisfied`) names the
      # released version here. A receipt without registry publishes, or no receipt, leaves the output empty and
      # skips the post-release smoke test.
      - name: Find the version this run released
        id: published
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version=$(scripts/released-version.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt/release-receipt.json")
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Summarize the receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          # Per attempt: a re-run keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing it.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-receipt
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 30

  # Installs the versions just published from the public registries into clean projects on each platform we ship
  # prebuilt binaries for, and uses them (scripts/smoke-published.sh). Needs no secrets and no write access. It
  # cannot undo a release: a failure here is the alarm that the published packages are broken.
  smoke-published:
    name: Smoke-test the published release (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: [release-candidate, execute]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the GitHub release notes for one michi version: every package's CHANGELOG section for it.

Usage: group-release-notes.py <version> [repo root]

Callisto attaches the group's one GitHub release (michi@{version}) to michi-core, so the page it writes holds only
michi-core's notes. Rust pipeline users and npm users would find nothing there. This joins each package's section
under its own heading, in the order a reader is most likely to look for it. A package whose section only says it was
released with the group is left out, and so is one with no section for the version.
"""

import pathlib
import re
import sys

PACKAGES = [
    ("michi-core (Rust)", "crates/michi-core/CHANGELOG.md"),
    ("michi-pipeline (Rust)", "crates/michi-pipeline/CHANGELOG.md"),
    ("michi-graph (Rust)", "crates/michi-graph/CHANGELOG.md"),
    ("@orin-dx/michi (npm)", "packages/michi-node/CHANGELOG.md"),
]

# The line Callisto writes for a fixed-group member with no changes of its own.
GROUP_ONLY = "- Released together with the `michi` fixed group."


def section(changelog: str, version: str) -> str:
    """The body under `## {version}`, up to the next `## ` heading, without the date/compare line."""
    lines = changelog.splitlines()
    start = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() == f"## {version}":
            start = i + 1
            break
    if start is None:
        return ""
    body = []
    for line in lines[start:]:
        if line.startswith("## "):
            break
        body.append(line)
    text = "\n".join(body).strip()
    # Callisto's `_date · [compare](...)_` line repeats per package; the release page has its own date.
    text = re.sub(r"\A_[^\n]*compare[^\n]*_\s*", "", text).strip()
    return text


def notes(version: str, root: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    parts = []
    for title, path in PACKAGES:
        file = root / path
        if not file.is_file():
            continue
        body = section(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), version)
        if not body or body == GROUP_ONLY:
            continue
        # Demote `### Minor Changes` and the like so they sit under the package heading.
        body = re.sub(r"^### ", "### ", body, flags=re.M).replace("\n### ", "\n#### ")
        if body.startswith("### "):
            body = "#" + body
        parts.append(f"## {title}\n\n{body}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts) + ("\n" if parts else "")


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) not in (2, 3):
        print(__doc__.strip().splitlines()[2], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) == 3 else pathlib.Path(".")
    sys.stdout.write(notes(sys.argv[1], root))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Self-test for group-release-notes.py. Run: python3 scripts/test_group_release_notes.py"""

import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

SCRIPT = pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name("group-release-notes.py")

CORE = """# michi-core

## 0.11.0

_2026-11-21 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/compare/michi@0.10.0...michi@0.11.0)_

### Minor Changes

- **Breaking:** core change.

## 0.10.0

- older core change.
"""

PIPELINE = """# michi-pipeline

## 0.11.0

_2026-11-21 · [compare](x)_

### Minor Changes

- pipeline change.

### Patch Changes

- pipeline fix.
"""

GRAPH = """# michi-graph

## 0.11.0

_2026-11-21 · [compare](x)_

- Released together with the `michi` fixed group.
"""

NODE = """# @orin-dx/michi

## 0.11.0

### Minor Changes

- js change.
"""


def run(version, files):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        root = pathlib.Path(tmp)
        for path, text in files.items():
            (root / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (root / path).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        out = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), version, str(root)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
        )
        return out.stdout, out.returncode


ALL = {
    "crates/michi-core/CHANGELOG.md": CORE,
    "crates/michi-pipeline/CHANGELOG.md": PIPELINE,
    "crates/michi-graph/CHANGELOG.md": GRAPH,
    "packages/michi-node/CHANGELOG.md": NODE,
}

EXPECTED = """## michi-core (Rust)

#### Minor Changes

- **Breaking:** core change.

## michi-pipeline (Rust)

#### Minor Changes

- pipeline change.

#### Patch Changes

- pipeline fix.

## @orin-dx/michi (npm)

#### Minor Changes

- js change.
"""

CASES = [
    # (name, version, files, expected stdout)
    ("every package with changes, group-only and older sections left out", "0.11.0", ALL, EXPECTED),
    ("a version no package has", "9.9.9", ALL, ""),
    ("a missing changelog is skipped", "0.11.0", {"packages/michi-node/CHANGELOG.md": NODE},
     "## @orin-dx/michi (npm)\n\n#### Minor Changes\n\n- js change.\n"),
    ("a version prefix of another is not matched", "0.1", ALL, ""),
]


def main():
    failed = 0
    for name, version, files, expected in CASES:
        stdout, code = run(version, files)
        if code != 0 or stdout != expected:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}: exit {code}\n--- got ---\n{stdout}--- expected ---\n{expected}")
    print(f"{len(CASES) - failed}/{len(CASES)} passed")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the GitHub release notes for one michi version: every package's CHANGELOG section for it.

Usage: group-release-notes.py <version> [repo root]

Callisto attaches the group's one GitHub release (michi@{version}) to michi-core, so the page it writes holds only
michi-core's notes. Rust pipeline users and npm users would find nothing there. This joins each package's section
under its own heading, in the order a reader is most likely to look for it. A package whose section only says it was
released with the group is left out, and so is one with no section for the version.
"""

import pathlib
import re
import sys

PACKAGES = [
    ("michi-core (Rust)", "crates/michi-core/CHANGELOG.md"),
    ("michi-pipeline (Rust)", "crates/michi-pipeline/CHANGELOG.md"),
    ("michi-graph (Rust)", "crates/michi-graph/CHANGELOG.md"),
    ("@orin-dx/michi (npm)", "packages/michi-node/CHANGELOG.md"),
]

# The line Callisto writes for a fixed-group member with no changes of its own.
GROUP_ONLY = "- Released together with the `michi` fixed group."


def section(changelog: str, version: str) -> str:
    """The body under `## {version}`, up to the next `## ` heading, without the date/compare line."""
    lines = changelog.splitlines()
    start = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() == f"## {version}":
            start = i + 1
            break
    if start is None:
        return ""
    body = []
    for line in lines[start:]:
        if line.startswith("## "):
            break
        body.append(line)
    text = "\n".join(body).strip()
    # Callisto's `_date · [compare](...)_` line repeats per package; the release page has its own date.
    text = re.sub(r"\A_[^\n]*compare[^\n]*_\s*", "", text).strip()
    return text


def notes(version: str, root: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    parts = []
    for title, path in PACKAGES:
        file = root / path
        if not file.is_file():
            continue
        body = section(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), version)
        if not body or body == GROUP_ONLY:
            continue
        # Demote `### Minor Changes` and the like so they sit under the package heading.
        body = re.sub(r"^### ", "### ", body, flags=re.M).replace("\n### ", "\n#### ")
        if body.startswith("### "):
            body = "#" + body
        parts.append(f"## {title}\n\n{body}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts) + ("\n" if parts else "")


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) not in (2, 3):
        print(__doc__.strip().splitlines()[2], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) == 3 else pathlib.Path(".")
    sys.stdout.write(notes(sys.argv[1], root))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

**What changes:**
- **Config:** `callisto.toml` goes from 38 lines to just the GitHub-release setting and the fixed group. Under 0.22 the release plan, tags and versions come out identical to before.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the cargo-semver-checks release type for the michi fixed group's pending changesets.

Only the YAML front matter of `.changeset/*.md` counts, and only entries naming a fixed-group package (the group
releases together, so any member's bump is everyone's). cargo-semver-checks
names release types literally, so before 1.0 Callisto's minor bump (0.4 -> 0.5) is `major` here.

Prints `infer` when no changeset names a fixed-group package: then the version in the manifests is the guide (on
Callisto's version PR the changesets are already applied and the versions bumped).

Usage: scripts/pending-release-type.py <current michi-core version> [changeset dir]
"""
...
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Print the version a Callisto release receipt shows as published to a registry, for the post-release smoke test.
#
# Usage: scripts/released-version.sh RECEIPT_JSON
#
# Prints the version, or an empty line when the receipt is missing or holds no registry publish (the smoke test is then
# skipped). Exits 1 when the receipt covers several versions, since the smoke test checks one. `published` is a publish
# that landed in this run; `alreadySatisfied` is one a re-run adopted from a failed earlier attempt.
set -euo pipefail

receipt="${1:?usage: released-version.sh RECEIPT_JSON}"
if [[ ! -f "$receipt" ]]; then
  echo
  exit 0
fi

96-## `[registries]`
97-
98:Keyed by registry name: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, not starting with `-`. Three registries are predeclared: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). They exist even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<predeclared>]` entry configures that registry and may leave `kind` out. Any other name fails with E325 when it is not a valid name, is a `publish-to` word (`github-release`, `none`), or is the old `cratesIo` spelling.
99-
100-| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
101-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
102-| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `crates-io`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321. A predeclared registry given another kind fails with E334 |
103-| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its URL from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a package publishes to the registry by naming it in `publish-to` |
104-| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
105-| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
106-| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |
107-
108-For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
109-
110-A named `kind = "npm"` or `kind = "pypi"` registry cannot be a `publish-to` target (E330). A named npm registry's `url` only approves a package's `publishConfig.registry`; a named pypi registry does nothing yet.
--
139-| `match` | string | required | `ecosystem/name`, or `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
140-| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
141:| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"github-release"` \| `"none"`, or a registry name: `"crates-io"`, `"npm"`, `"pypi"` or a `kind = "cargo"` `[registries]` entry) | none | Where this package publishes. Any other value fails with E330 |

"""

import pathlib
import re
import sys

GROUP = {"michi-core", "michi-graph", "michi-pipeline", "michi-node", "@orin-dx/michi"}
RANK = {"none": 0, "patch": 1, "minor": 2, "major": 3}


def front_matter_bumps(text: str):
    """(package, level) pairs from a changeset's front matter, or nothing if it has none."""
    match = re.match(r"\A---[ \t]*\r?\n(.*?)\r?\n---[ \t]*(\r?\n|\Z)", text, re.S)
    if not match:
        return []
    bumps = []
    for line in match.group(1).splitlines():
        entry = re.match(r"""^\s*["']?([^"':]+?)["']?\s*:\s*["']?(major|minor|patch|none)["']?\s*$""", line)
        if entry:
            bumps.append((entry.group(1), entry.group(2)))
    return bumps


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    version = sys.argv[1]
    directory = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ".changeset")
    level = None
    for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.md")):
        for package, bump in front_matter_bumps(path.read_text()):
            if package in GROUP and (level is None or RANK[bump] > RANK[level]):
                level = bump
    if level is None:
        print("infer")
    elif level == "major" or (level == "minor" and version.startswith("0.")):
        print("major")
    elif level == "minor":
        print("minor")
    else:
        print("patch")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks the API of michi-core, michi-pipeline and michi-graph against crates.io at the release type their pending
# changes call for.
#
# Callisto computes the pending bump (`callisto status`); the fixed group gives every member the same one, so
# michi-core's stands for all. cargo-semver-checks names release types literally, so before 1.0 Callisto's minor bump
# (0.4 -> 0.5) is `major` here. With nothing pending, the version bump is the guide: on Callisto's version PR the
# changesets are already applied and the manifests carry the new version.
set -euo pipefail

status=$(callisto --format json status)
severity=$(jq -r '.packages[] | select(.package == "cargo/michi-core") | .pendingSeverity // "none"' <<<"$status")
version=$(jq -r '.packages[] | select(.package == "cargo/michi-core") | .currentVersion' <<<"$status")

case "$severity" in
  none | null) release_type=infer ;;
  major) release_type=major ;;
  minor) if [[ "$version" == 0.* ]]; then release_type=major; else release_type=minor; fi ;;
  patch) release_type=patch ;;
  *)
    echo "unexpected pending severity from callisto: $severity" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

if [[ "$release_type" == infer ]]; then
  echo "Nothing pending for michi: checking against the version bump (michi-core $version)"
  cargo semver-checks check-release -p michi-core -p michi-pipeline -p michi-graph
else
  echo "Pending release type: $release_type (Callisto: $severity, michi-core $version)"
  cargo semver-checks check-release -p michi-core -p michi-pipeline -p michi-graph --release-type "$release_type"
fi

  cargo semver-checks check-release -p michi-core -p michi-pipeline -p michi-graph

  cargo semver-checks check-release -p michi-core -p michi-pipeline -p michi-graph --release-type "$release_type"

lines: +**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to build an already-done report and the one place to add hints to a status report. The duplicate function and hint channel are removed.
+- `already_done(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` enum are removed, at `michi_core::resilience` and at the crate root: match on your stored `Option` yourself.

+- `StatusResponse::hints(vec)` and its `hints` field are removed: `StatusResponse::new(..).hints(h).render()` → `AgentResponse::new("status").status(s).hints(h).render(OutputFormat::Text)`. `StatusResponse::render()` stays, without a `help` line.
+A response cuts table cells over 200 characters by default; add `.truncate_cells_at(usize::MAX)` for the old uncut text.

+**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to render an error, a batch's outcomes, pipeline state, a status report or an already-done report. The standalone functions that duplicated it are removed. Below, `r` is `new AgentResponse(name)`.
+- `renderDomainError(code, message, hints, false, causes)` → `r.error(code, message, causes)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
+- `renderPartialSuccess(completed, failed, skipped)` → `r.partialSuccess('partial_success', completed, failed, skipped)`, then `r.renderText()`.
+- `renderStatus(toolName, description, items, hints)` → `r.status(toolName, description, items)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
+- `renderAlreadyDone(operation, summary, hints)` → `r.alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
+- `alreadyDone(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` type are removed: check your stored result yourself (`stored != null`).

+The replacements also give you `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()`. Like any response, they cut a table cell over 200 characters and list it in the `truncated` block; the removed functions never cut.

content.text:
A semver check isn't strictly needed. Here is what it does, so you can decide.

**What it does:** the CI job runs cargo-semver-checks, comparing the Rust crates' public API with the versions on crates.io. It fails when a PR breaks the API but its changesets only ask for a bump that doesn't allow a break.

**What that protects in michi:** before 1.0, every minor release is allowed to break, and almost every michi release is a minor. So the check only bites in one case: a breaking change hidden in a **patch** release, as 0.7.1 was. In that case it's the only thing stopping a user who runs `cargo update` from getting broken code.

**What it costs:** a CI job on every PR, plus the plumbing to ask Callisto for the pending bump. It doesn't cover the npm package.

**My recommendation:** keep it. It's cheap now (one shell script calling `callisto status`, no Python), and patch releases do happen. If you'd rather keep CI small, dropping it is fine before 1.0 if every release is a minor. I'd then add it back before 1.0, when patch releases matter more.

Meanwhile the finding on change #53 is fixed and pushed to #141 (`58363219`). Each error cause is now charged like a hint (its text plus 1 byte), not text plus 24, so a full 10,000-cause report fits a fresh builder again. The new test fails with the exact error from the finding when the old charge is put back. The output-size guarantee still holds across all 14 output-bound tests. `just check` passes. All 1,191 non-scaling Rust tests and 183 Node tests pass, and the 18 scaling tests pass when run alone. They failed in the full run only because the machine's load average was 155.

Both findings you asked about are resolved, but a new medium finding on #141 needs your call before I touch the NAPI limits.

**Already resolved:**
- **Low, semver script:** resolved as moot. Commit `fb3cdab6` removes `check-semver.sh`, the `check-api` recipe and the semver CI job from #140, and #140's description now says so. `actionlint` and `just check` pass.
- **Medium, error causes:** fixed in `58363219` and resolved.

**New: removing `renderPipeline` makes some very large reports impossible to render.**
- **The case:** 10,000 pipeline steps with 1,660-byte names fit the per-call 16 MiB string limit. Through `AgentResponse`, the same report also pays a fixed charge for every row, so it goes over 16 MiB and throws. Partial success and status have the same issue.
- **Why it isn't the same quick fix as causes:** that per-row charge isn't a mistake. It's what stops a JS caller adding millions of empty rows across many calls and running the process out of memory. Lowering it would weaken that protection.
- **The proper fix:** keep strings capped at 16 MiB as now, which preserves the capacity of any single call, and count the per-row structure against a separate cap. The documented output guarantee would become 19 × string bytes + a fixed amount per row + 4 KiB, still under V8's string limit. That changes the published NAPI limits and the output-bound tests, about a day's careful work.
- **Alternative:** accept it. Only reports near 16 MB are affected, and they now fail with a clear error before anything renders. Resolve the finding with that reasoning.

I recommend the proper fix in #141 before 0.12, so going through `AgentResponse` never drops a report the old functions accepted.

input.prompt:
Fix a review finding in michi's NAPI byte accounting. Repo orin-dx/michi. Work on the existing branch `refactor/one-render-path` (PR #141): `git fetch origin refactor/one-render-path` and check it out (create a local branch tracking it; its head is 58363219 or later). Read AGENTS.md and PRINCIPLES.md (prefix shell commands with `rtk`; `cargo nextest run`; no unwrap/expect in lib; comments plain, wrapped at 120 cols; every claim needs a test that fails when broken — prove with a mutant and revert). Commit (`fix(napi): ...`, no session links or Claude-Session trailers) and push to `refactor/one-render-path` (normal push; never force; never main). Do not open PRs. `just check`/`just test` must run outside the sandbox (moon locks .git/config).

## The finding (Medium, crates/michi-core/src/napi/outcome.rs:147)
"Removing `renderPipeline` leaves no way to render some previously valid reports: 10,000 pending steps with five-byte IDs and 1,660-byte ASCII names pass the 16 MiB input check (`napi/input.rs:394–405`, `napi/response.rs:478–484`), but row and truncation bookkeeping push even a fresh builder over the cumulative cap (`response.rs:232–240, 304–310`). The replacement throws instead of returning a table with truncated cells; the same cumulative check affects the partial-success and status replacements (`response.rs:297–324`). Preserve the former single-report input capacity while keeping a separate bound on retained data and rendered output."

Context: PR #141 removed the standalone JS renderers (renderPipeline, renderPartialSuccess, renderStatus, renderAlreadyDone, renderDomainError) so AgentResponse is the one path. `JsAgentResponse` holds a cumulative `held` total (strings plus structural charges: ROW_OVERHEAD/OUTCOME_ROW memory per row, SECTION_OVERHEAD, ERROR_OVERHEAD, HINT_OVERHEAD, `cost::table_repeats` for names a `truncated`/`totalCount` table writes again) capped at `input::MAX_INPUT_BYTES` (16 MiB). The documented guarantee (response.rs ~:138, napi/cost.rs header, napi/input.rs) is that a render is at most 19x the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface (text, JSON, toCallToolResult) and stays under V8's string limit; `crates/michi-core/src/napi/response/output_bound.rs` measures it over a matrix of hostile responses. A sibling fix already landed (58363219): error causes are charged text+HINT_OVERHEAD instead of text+String overhead.

## Required outcome (all must hold)
1. Every single call that passes its own per-call checks succeeds on a fresh `AgentResponse` (items, kvItems, partialSuccess, pipeline, status, alreadyDone, error, and the hint/recovery/humanContent setters), including the finding's case (10,000 pending steps, 5-byte ids, 1,660-byte names) and the equivalent worst cases for partialSuccess and status. Add tests for each that fail on today's code.
2. Retained memory stays bounded: many calls cannot accumulate unbounded rows/cells (keep the protection ROW_OVERHEAD exists for, e.g. repeated `items(Array(100000).fill([]), ...)`).
3. Rendered output stays bounded and under V8's max string length on every surface; restate the guarantee precisely in the docs (response.rs AgentResponse doc, cost.rs header, input.rs constants) and keep `output_bound.rs` proving it (extend the matrix with the new worst cases, including maximal structure + maximal strings together).
4. No response accepted today is rejected afterwards (don't make any limit stricter).
The finding's suggested shape: keep strings capped at 16 MiB cumulative (so one call's worth of strings always fits) and count structural/bookkeeping charges against a separate cap sized so that 19x(strings) + (structure's real output multiplier)x(structure) + 4 KiB stays under V8's limit. Derive the structure cap and its multiplier from the writers, not by guessing; if a single combined cap with headroom is cleaner and provably meets 1-4, that's acceptable — explain the choice. Error messages for the new cap must name it clearly (e.g. `cumulative structure total N exceeds maximum of M`); keep the existing `cumulative byte total` message for strings.

## Docs/changeset
Update packages/michi-node/README.md and docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md where the limits are described. Add one bullet to `.changeset/js-one-render-path.md` (user-first, JS terms) only if the visible limit behaviour changes for JS users (e.g. "any report a single call accepts now fits a new `AgentResponse`"); do not edit other changesets.

## Verify (exit codes)
`just check`, `just test` (scaling tests are wall-clock and flake under load; if only `michi-core::scaling` fails, rerun it alone and report `uptime`), the output-bound tests, and a mutant per new guarantee (e.g. charge structure against the string cap again → the finding's test fails; drop the structure cap → a retained-memory test fails).

## Report
Commit SHA; the design (caps, constants, how the output bound is derived and its new formula); tests added and their mutants; check exit codes; anything that couldn't be met. Under ~700 words.

Structure is row, cell and String storage, section and error overheads, the hint/cause/recovery allowances, the type name, and the repeats from `table_repeats` and `fixed_table_repeats`. The new message is `cumulative held total N exceeds maximum of 27262976`.
- Every charge is the same number of bytes as before; I only sorted each into strings or structure, with a `Charge {strings, structure}` per slot. So the measured 19x factor still applies to the held total.
- **New bound:** a render is at most 19 × held + 4 KiB, which is at most 19 × 26 MiB + 4 KiB = 494 MiB on every surface. That stays under V8's limit of 2^29 − 24, checked by a compile-time assert. 26 is the largest whole MiB that does (27 would be 513 MiB).

**Why one cap on the sum rather than a separate structure cap:** before this change, responses holding up to 16 MiB of pure structure were accepted (e.g. six `items(Array(100000).fill([]))` calls). Requirement 1 can't hold for every call with the current per-call checks:
- **Calls with long names and many cut cells.** The names written again for each cut cell are not limited per call. A pipeline with a 4 KiB section name and 20,000 cut cells charges 82 MB of repeats, and its render can't fit under V8's limit at all. These calls stay rejected, as they were before.

The replacements also give you `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()`. Like any response, they cut a table cell over 200 characters and list it in the `truncated` block; the removed functions never cut.

New: `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)` returns a GitHub Actions annotation, `::error title={code}::{message}`, on one line.
835:- **The byte budget bounds the output (16 MiB, was 64 MiB).** The 64 MiB budget limited input only. A control character renders to 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON and 19 in `toCallToolResult()`, so 64 MiB of input could produce 1.2 GiB, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. Measured in Node before the change (60 one-MiB control-character values): `renderText()` 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS, 2.4 s; `renderJson()` rendered, then threw `GenericFailure`, 1.6 GiB RSS; `toCallToolResult()` 25 s, 3.2 GiB. At 16 MiB the worst render is 19 x 16 MiB = 304 MiB, under V8's limit, so a response renders or is rejected by the budget before any rendering. A `const` assertion ties the cap to the string limit, and a unit test pins the factor 19 for every ASCII byte. Considered: charging each control character at its escaped size (exact, but it adds a second accounting table that must follow every escape rule, and plain ASCII gains nothing), and an estimate-then-render check in each render (the budget already is that estimate).
836:- **Compatibility:** inputs over 16 MiB of strings per call, or per `AgentResponse`, are now rejected where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Pre-1.0, and no known consumer sends that much; the error names the cap.

content.text:
I fixed the `renderPipeline` finding on change #54 in #141 and resolved it on the trail.

- **Limits:** anything a single call accepts now fits a new `AgentResponse`. Strings keep their 16 MiB cap, which equals the per-call cap, so one call's strings always fit. Strings plus row storage and bookkeeping get a separate 26 MiB cap.
- **Output bound:** a render stays at most 19 × what's held + 4 KiB, which is 494 MiB at most, under V8's string limit. A compile-time check fails the build if the cap is ever raised past that.
- **Tests:** there are fit tests for the reported 10,000-step pipeline and for the worst partial-success, status, items, key-value and error cases. Each fails when the old single cap is put back, and removing the new cap fails the memory-protection tests. Nothing accepted before is now rejected.
- **One case still not covered:** a very long section name repeated for every cut cell can still be rejected, because nothing limits it per call. Such a render could exceed V8's limit anyway. This is written up in `06-decisions.md`.
- **My checks:** `just check` and `just test` pass (1,235 Rust and 184 Node tests). I added the decision entry (`1fe980f2`), and #141's description and the JS changeset note the new limit.

Every review finding on #140 and #141 is now resolved or dismissed. Release PR #131 is still waiting for you to merge it.

content.text:
It was a new finding, not a missed push. Change #54 was already at `1fe980f2` with the earlier finding resolved; the reviewer's next pass found a different edge case. It's now fixed in `907839a1`, pushed, and resolved on the trail.

- **The bug:** `AgentResponse.pipeline(name, …)` and `.partialSuccess(name, …)` counted the section name against the call's 16 MiB string budget. The removed functions took no name, so a payload of exactly 16 MiB that they accepted now threw over 4 bytes.
- **The fix:** the name is checked on its own, still capped at 4 KiB, and counted as structure, the same as the type name. The output bound still covers it.
- **The sweep:** I checked every replacement against the function it replaced. `status`, `alreadyDone` and `error` take no new argument and no longer count hints, so they accept everything their old versions did. This edge case can't come back through those.
- **Tests:** a Rust test for the 16 MiB partial-success payload, and a Node test of the finding's 16-step case, which goes through the JS method's per-call check. Each fails when its half of the fix is reverted. A Rust test of the pipeline case passes either way, because the pipeline's stored total never counted its status strings. The Node test is the one that guards the pipeline.
- **Checks:** `just check` and `just test` pass (1,237 Rust and 185 Node tests).

result: The new finding on change #54 is fixed (`907839a1`) and resolved: section names no longer count against the 16 MiB string budget, and a sweep confirmed no other replacement has the gap. Release PR #131 still waits on you.
